newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at 7-year high on electronics.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at 7-year high on electronics.

text.p: Taiwan share prices surged to a seven-year high close despite late profit-taking on Tuesday as the trendsetting electronics sector attracted heavy buying.
The index surged as high as 8,763.88 and ended at 8,679.24, a gain of 38.79 points or 0.45 percent. It was the fourth rise in as many sessions for the weighted index.
Tuesday's close surpassed a seven-year closing high of 8,661.72 recorded on April 26. The index has not closed higher since ending at 8,922.67 on May 9, 1990.
Tuesday's intraday high of 8,763.88 also surpassed a seven-year intraday high of 8,758.41 set on April 10.
Turnover was a heavy T$191.3 billion, a two-month high.
"Fearing a likely fourth straight session of gains may be too much for the near term, investors turned conservative in late trade," said United Securities analyst Lin Long-hsien.
Electronics surged 3.60 percent, with leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor up T$6.5 to T$108.5 and rival chipmaker United Semiconductor up T$2.5 to T$90.5.

"The strong ones are always strong," Lin said. "Investors are forced to buy electronics because they have seen that recently if you buy electronics, you earn money, but if you buy others, you lose money."

Brokers said investors had come to see electronics as a locomotive leading the overall index to new highs and have gradually accepted a higher price-earnings ratio for what once were seen as relatively high-risk investments, brokers said.
"Since electronics have the best outlook among Taiwan's industries, investors now can accept higher price-earnings ratios for the sector," said independent analyst Michael Hung.

In the past, the market had tolerated P/E ratios at around 20, below the broader market average. Brokers said that perception has changed as the sector has matured, and investors now accept P/E ratios of 30.
